items.title: Cortex-M3 event register omission
items.condition: Interrupt pending before WFE may miss an event.
items.handling: The reviewed software slice offers no WFE low-power policy.

items.title: Flash read after WFI or WFE
items.condition: Sleep may disrupt reads when using two wait states and prefetch with the Flash interface clock gated.
items.handling: HSI8 uses zero wait states. PLL72 requires the Flash interface gate and retains it. The reviewed run path leaves Stop and Standby outside this scope.

items.title: DBGMCU debug registers inaccessible to user firmware
items.condition: Ordinary firmware may observe zero for DBGMCU_IDCODE and DBGMCU_CR.
items.handling: Flash-size halfword provides a capacity check. Physical revision and debug freeze belong to the external probe.

items.title: Flash memory BSY latency after STRT
items.condition: BSY can read clear on the first bus cycle after starting page erase.
items.handling: Complete and read back the control write before polling status. The controller then requires EOP without an error flag and verifies the page.

items.title: LSI clock stabilization time
items.condition: The oscillator can remain outside the specified frequency range after LSIRDY asserts.
items.handling: Wait 128 nominal microseconds after LSIRDY on the selected HSI8 timebase. Observe an owned clock request and settle it before irreversible activation.

items.title: SPI2 master and USART3 synchronous clock
items.condition: SPI2 software NSS prevents the synchronous USART3 clock on PB12.
items.handling: The short-poll profile uses PB12 as software CS. No USART3 synchronous controller is admitted.

items.title: I2C2 SMBA and SPI2 NSS share PB12
items.condition: I2C2 enabled can take ownership of PB12 when it is an alternate function output.
items.handling: SPI2 uses a GPIO software CS. The fixture selects I2C1 and no I2C2 controller.

items.title: Remapped SPI1 master and I2C1 SMBA conflict
items.condition: Remapped SPI1 PB5 MOSI conflicts with I2C1 SMBA when both peripheral clocks are on.
items.handling: The closed software slice uses SPI2 and the default I2C1. No SPI1 remap is defined.

items.title: DMA channel disable and transfer error when clearing the global flag
items.condition: A simultaneous transfer error and whole-channel flag clear may leave the channel enabled and hide TEIF.
items.handling: Withdraw the USART DMA request, disable and verify the channel, inspect late TEIF, then clear individual TCIF, HTIF and TEIF flags with an aligned 32-bit IFCR write. Section 2.4.2 requires aligned 32-bit DMA register accesses.

items.title: RVU remains set at low APB clock frequency
items.condition: An APB frequency below twice the IWDG clock can prevent the reload update flag from clearing.
items.handling: Admit the live HSI8 / APB1 8 MHz clock before activation. Bound the RVU wait and retain the irreversible owner on failure.

items.title: PVU remains set at low APB clock frequency
items.condition: An APB frequency below twice the IWDG clock can prevent the prescaler update flag from clearing.
items.handling: Require the same reviewed APB1 clock and wait for both PVU and RVU before verifying the nominal settings.

items.title: RVU and PVU remain set in Stop mode
items.condition: Entering Stop immediately after updating the watchdog registers can leave update flags pending.
items.handling: Wait for both shadow flags in Run and retain irreversible effects on failure. This mode does not expose Stop.

items.title: I2C byte events must precede the next transfer
items.condition: Late software handling can duplicate, miss or introduce bytes.
items.handling: Hold SCL where ACK/STOP ordering requires a dedicated window and wait for BTF for longer reads and controller writes.

items.title: I2C receive data may corrupt around STOP
items.condition: Delayed final DR reads can corrupt the final received byte.
items.handling: The two-byte and longer receive paths hold SCL across the critical DR/STOP sequence.

items.title: SMBus cannot always NACK an invalid payload
items.condition: The hardware cannot satisfy every SMBus v2.0 acknowledgment contract.
items.handling: The admitted mode is a seven-bit I2C polling controller without SMBus.

items.title: Misplaced I2C STOP inhibits a new START
items.condition: A misplaced STOP can stall SB detection or make an attempted START report BERR.
items.handling: Bound the wait for SB. A failed pending START enters a local reset using CR1.SWRST; the owner must explicitly recover.

items.title: I2C repeated START timing at 88 to 100 kHz
items.condition: Master standard mode can violate repeated START setup when a target stretches or the SCL rise exceeds the rated margin.
items.handling: Admit the exact nominal 80 kHz HSI8 profile, with APB1-8MHz CR2 FREQ 8, CCR 50 and TRISE 9.

items.title: I2C slave data valid time can be late
items.condition: Slave transmit with no clock stretching can miss data timing without OVR.
items.handling: The slice admits only the polling master role.

items.title: Analog I2C filters can hold BUSY after local reset
items.condition: A stuck analog filter needs externally safe electrical transitions before reset can clear BUSY.
items.handling: Local recovery uses CR1.SWRST and verified idle lines. Persistent BUSY remains an error; this fixture does not issue unqualified GPIO recovery pulses.

items.title: USART idle frame detection at receiver clock deviation
items.condition: Clock mismatch can prevent detection of IDLE.
items.handling: The initial USART2 mode owns a byte IRQ ring; it does not depend on IDLE or promise gap timing.

items.title: USART transmit can clear receiver parity error
items.condition: With parity enabled in full duplex, a data-register write can clear the receiver PE flag.
items.handling: The initial USART2 mode uses 8N1. Production parity modes require a separate review.

items.title: SPI slave CRC may accumulate even with NSS high
items.condition: The SPI slave CRC can observe the shared clock while the slave is unselected.
items.handling: This mode selects controller polling without hardware CRC or slave operation.

items.title: SPI CRC is sensitive to another device on the same DMA channel
items.condition: Simultaneous DMA traffic on a shared request channel can corrupt SPI CRC.
items.handling: SPI2 short-poll claims neither DMA nor hardware CRC.

limitations: IWDG activation is reviewed under HSI8 only. Its board supply does not admit DS5319 Table 25 oscillator bounds, and this mode exposes no Stop path.
Source review covers GPIO, USART2 8N1 IRQ byte queue and opt-in halfword/page Flash under HSI8 or the reviewed 8 MHz MCO bypass and PLL72.
This audit indexes selected sections for the maintained slice; other ES096 sections and other F1 groups are not admitted by this profile.
No physical silicon cut, oscillator accuracy, board wiring, timings, DMA, remap, low-power or physical qualification is established.
Low-, high- and XL-density software references select GPIO output, USART2 IRQ and HSI8. Additional modes require their exact package and errata reviews.
F100, F101, F102, F105 and F107 exact software references select HSI8, GPIO output and USART2 IRQ byte events.
F100 high-density, F101 low/high/XL-density and F102 low-density software references select HSI8, GPIO output and USART2 IRQ byte events.
